answer: Sybil resistance comes from making coordinated equivocation costly: when k identities produce correlated conflicting attestations, pairwise evidence exposes up to k(k−1)/2 culpable pairs, so slashing grows as O(k^2), not linearly. A swarm therefore cannot dilute blame across aliases; detection applies an exponential multiplier to capital loss against bonded collateral, with asymmetric depreciation amplifying the penalty. A vertex joining the jade meadow gains no protection from splitting its stake among identities.
